appearance.observation: Separate portrait, header and note tracks restore the side portraits at f2. At f0 the source status marks fan outward while the candidate uses a soft translation. The f3 source tag and downward label streak still read earlier.
At f22 the three portrait disks, centered note and first two inbox rows retain the held layout. The portrait artwork is independently rendered.

Named Eleanor and Charlotte anchors agree through acceleration. The late fit tracks both the rising rows and the change in spacing and scale. Darla and El align at f95 and the leading Margot row is visible again at f101. The home bar and the strength of the departing streak around f56 still differ.

The opening and settled badge use separate measured dimensions. At f108 the leftmost original glyph is darker and the trailing part is more displaced. The independently drawn card illustration still has visibly wider pink shapes.
The fitted rim and pad improve the shape and lower light. The f136 island and rainbow edge still bend and spread differently. The held lower-right wash and rim contrast at f150 differ.

The candidate opens on ‘For’ and layers the arriving disks under the outgoing title at f212. Around f180, parts of the second line brighten in a different order and several of the tiny incoming patches remain fainter at f212.

The first visible hull bottom and the later rim are closer after fitting the clipped edge. On f316–319 the source keyboard is already sharper and vertically registered differently while the candidate streak persists.

The detached controls sit under the suggestion at f394, and the pointer reaches the Send? capsule from below.

The lower calendar band is visible at f397 with the suggestion still above it. Appointments rise through consecutive frames; by f403 the calendar has replaced the suggestion. The padded cursor follows the measured turn around f408–415 and lands beside the lower appointment.
At f435 the violet appointment remains above cyan through their overlap. The grid stays registered.
At f460 cyan sits below the violet appointment on the same calendar grid.
The ring tile leads at f478, then red and blue enter. The source still has a stronger violet block behind the ring and different holes in the outgoing calendar grid.
Individual centers and depth changes keep the four glyphs readable. At f536 and f612 the dark tile has different scale and edge softness, and the red and blue artwork and overlap edges still differ.
Separate tile paths and a fitted glow move downward together. Motion streaks persist on the last occupied frame f621, and f622–623 are blank. The tile edge blur differs locally.
The visible bottom at f624 and the detached pointer are much closer. At f626–632 the candidate body and keyboard are streaked longer, and the settled bottom and keyboard proportions still differ.

No and Yes become visible on f648 and f650. In the sampled fast approach, the chip and fitted pointer follow separate measured paths, with the tip just above the composer at f665–667 and nearly at Yes by f674.

The decoded tip has zero gap to Yes at f675. Rim and interior offsets follow the late retreat and keep the chip and tip registered through f695. The keyboard keys and surrounding bubble type still differ.
Width and height are separately fitted from the first squash to the held badge. The held center card and heart proportions still differ visibly at f703–708.
Each word has separate measured bounds and opacity. ‘The’ reads first at f717, ‘iMessage’ enters on f741, and the complete second line is in place by the final set pose. Wash falloff is approximate.
Both movies reduce exposure into the final black frame at f777 and share the 40 ms final hold.
